name: Axion1-0/Axion-1.0-35B reproduction checkpoint card
notes: Fetched 2026-11-10 (4,556-byte card). Repo created 2026-10-16, 1,125 downloads / 70 likes at crawl. Card title is 'Axion 1.0-35B - Reproduction' and the body says it is 'a reproduction checkpoint of Axion 1.0-35B, following the recipe described in Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified'. Citation block lists Yuqi Jia, Yunjie Tian, Jiayu Zheng, Yijun Liang, Jingchen Sun, Mengyu Zhao, Di Fu; eprint 2611.03233; code at github.com/bytedance/axion1_0. This is a third-party reproduction repo, not the paper authors' own release, and that distinction matters for how much weight the numbers carry. Model overview table: MoE, 'approximately 35B total, 3B active', BF16. Recipe: ~18K SFT examples, three stages (learn to reason / learn to investigate / learn through interaction via RL). Performance table prints paper-vs-reproduction side by side with six benchmarks: HLE, BMB, SEAL-0, HiPhO, FS Olympiad, FS Research. Reproduction 52.8 / 35.3 / 60.4 / 45.9 / 85.0 / 55.0 vs paper 52.2 / 35.3 / 62.2 / 45.7 / 86.0 / 56.7. Three rows degrade, three hold or improve. Footnote defines BMB as the human-difficult BioMysteryBench subset and FS as FrontierScience. Comparator columns: Agents-A1, Kimi-K2.6, DeepSeek-V4-Pro (Preview), Apodex 1.1 (ReAct and Agent Team), GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Muse-Spark-1.0, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5. All except Agents-A1 and Kimi-K2.6 are closed models whose numbers are taken from elsewhere. Serving: vLLM with --tensor-parallel-size 8, --max-model-len 131072, --reasoning-parser qwen3, --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder. The card states eight GPUs for the documented example.
